claims.text: SPS produces a uniquely refined microstructure in non-equilibrium Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys.
The SPS-produced microstructure is rich in metastable Mg-rich intermetallic compounds.
High-temperature oxidation and corrosive exposure transform the metastable phases into more stable compounds.
The phase transformations promote formation of a coherent protective oxide scale.
The protective oxide scale consists primarily of MgO and Al2O3.
The evolved microstructure improves corrosion resistance relative to the as-SPS state.
The evolved microstructure improves high-temperature oxidation behavior relative to the as-SPS state.
The initial SPS-produced alloy contains both metastable and stable intermetallic compounds.
The initial alloy has a density below 6 g/cm3.
Conventional induction-melted comparison alloys do not exhibit the same non-equilibrium microstructural features as the SPS alloys.
Rapid SPS minimizes diffusion and traps metastable phases.
Thermal or corrosive exposure causes transformation of the trapped metastable phases.
The phase transformation favors segregation of Mg and Al.
Segregated Mg and Al form protective MgO and Al2O3 layers.
The MgO and Al2O3 layers enhance corrosion resistance and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Exposure of the SPS alloy will result in lower corrosion current density than in the initial SPS-processed state.
Exposure of the SPS alloy will result in more stable and reduced oxidation weight gain.
Temperatures above approximately 800°C are sufficiently aggressive to drive the proposed phase transformations and oxide-scale formation.
Constituent-property differences predispose the alloy to form stable intermetallic compounds.
